Credits

Father Hanley’s, and I believe ‘Bit O’ Ginger’ jigs were contributed to the collection. It is doubtful but possible that Tommy Sullivan did compose it. I have never seen it in any older collection. (Bit O Ginger was contributed by Paddy Killoran)

The House in the Glen

This is transcribed as a slide in Johnny Leary’s book #253 (while it was played at a pace a bit slower than some of his jigs). He plays from low ACE for the second triplet, which sounds great! There is another transcription with this name, as a jig: https://thesession.org/tunes/12849 . But the settings here are closer to Johnny Leary’s.

↳ Posted by brailsford on October 25th, 2021.

The House in the Glen, X:14

This setting is based on Denis Doody’s playing from https://thesession.org/recordings/1309. It’s ended up in Gmaj after tweaking its pitch. This setting is close to Johnny Leary’s (except Johnny’s setting is in Amaj in his book). It is also close to the Monks of the Screw’s version (also in G, with the low G sounded). They also call it the House in the Glen.
Likely source? Pádraig O‘Keeffe of course. Here are links to the ITMA site which has transcriptions of settings he gave to pupils, in G with the same name. As for dates, the O’Connell manuscript dates from 1931 to 1962, with most in the mid 1940s. So it might predate the O’Brien publication.
https://www.itma.ie/digital-library/score/padraig_okeeffe_oconnell_ms_155
https://www.itma.ie/digital-library/score/padraig-okeeffe-ms-bk-2-4

↳ Posted by brailsford on February 11th, 2022.
